narrative:
Based on your application, the model has determined that you represent a higher-than-acceptable credit risk, leading to the denial of your loan. Your application showed a 56% probability of being a bad credit risk, meaning the model found more factors pointing toward potential repayment issues than toward a reliable history.

The most significant factor in this decision was your credit history. While you have paid off all your debts at this bank, this specific category is actually quite rare among approved applicants, with only about 3% of them sharing this profile. The model interpreted this as a less established credit pattern compared to the majority of approved borrowers, who typically have existing paid loans or other credit references. This pushed the decision toward denial.

Your checking account status was the second most influential factor. Your account is currently in the negative (below zero Deutsche Marks), which is a situation seen in only about 20% of approved applicants. Most approved borrowers have a positive balance or at least a zero balance, so this negative status signaled financial strain and contributed strongly to the unfavorable prediction.

On a positive note, your installment rate—the percentage of your income going toward loan payments—was actually a point in your favor. At just 1% of your disposable income, this is much lower than the average of nearly 3% among approved applicants. This factor worked against the denial, suggesting you could comfortably manage monthly payments. However, it was not strong enough to overcome the concerns raised by your credit history and account status.

Other aspects of your profile also added to the risk assessment. You are currently unemployed, a status held by only about 5% of approved applicants, and you are renting your home, while over 75% of approved borrowers own their property. Your request for a new car loan is also a common purpose among approved applicants, but combined with your other financial circumstances, it did not help your case.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a more conventional credit history by taking out and repaying smaller loans, and work on stabilizing your checking account to maintain a positive balance. Securing stable employment and building savings would also significantly strengthen your application. Addressing these areas will help you align more closely with the profile of applicants who are typically approved.
